shape.text: A Zendesk API token is sent as Basic authentication whose username is the account email address followed by /token and whose password is the token, so the documented credential string has the form {email_address}/token:{api_token}.
A capture of Zendesk's Security and authentication page from 2022-12-03 documents the same Basic credential composition as the page read in 2026.

The example credential on Zendesk's Security and authentication page has a 40-character letters-and-digits token part, has been unchanged since at least 2022-12-03, and is not declared representative of issued tokens.
No prefix, alphabet or length of a Zendesk API token is established by Zendesk.

unresolved.reason: The pages read state none and show only one example of 40 characters; two scanner rule artifacts agree on 40 characters but that records consistency between them, not a provider rule. A Zendesk statement of the token format, or an issued sample under a maintainer's authority, would settle it; neither was sought.

issuance.text: API tokens are created in Admin Center under Apps and integrations, APIs, Zendesk API; several can be active at once, up to 256 tokens (2048 for accounts that already had more), and deleting a token deactivates it permanently.
Accounts created on or after 2026-07-28 cannot create or use API tokens, and existing accounts lose the ability to create new API tokens from 2026-10-27.

lifecycle.text: Zendesk labels the API token deprecated and is retiring Support API tokens in three phases: inactivity deactivation on 2026-07-28, no new tokens for existing accounts on 2026-10-27, and permanent deactivation of all remaining tokens on 2027-04-30.

Deprecation, the restriction on new tokens and the final shutdown are separate events: existing active tokens continue to work after the restriction until 2027-04-30 unless they become inactive first.
A capture of Zendesk's Security and authentication page from 2026-04-21 still recommended API tokens or OAuth tokens over basic authentication and did not label the token deprecated.
Zendesk gives the lack of expiry, the lack of scope restriction and the lack of application binding as the reasons for retiring API tokens.
Whether the 2026-07-28 phase has been applied, and the date the retirement was announced, are not established.

unresolved.reason: The migration page read after 2026-07-28 still words the first phase as taking effect and gives no announcement date; the only dated bounds are the 2026-04-21 and 2026-09-24 captures. A Zendesk status statement or changelog entry would settle it.

collisions.text: An OAuth access token is a different credential in the same account, sent as an Authorization: Bearer value and stated to be up to 184 characters long, whereas an API token is a Basic password paired with an email address.
An API token is not associated with a specific Zendesk user, yet requests must supply the email address of a valid user, whose role limits what the token can do.
Whether and when Basic authentication with the account email and password is retired is not established.

unresolved.reason: The page names basic authentication together with API tokens as something to migrate away from, but gives no separate schedule for the password form. A Zendesk statement would settle it.

openQuestions.text: Whether API tokens of different eras differ in length or alphabet is not established.

unresolved.reason: Neither the provider pages nor the two rule artifacts read say so, and the documentation example has not changed since 2022. A Zendesk statement would settle it.
